Both round-1 minors are genuinely fixed in the shipped file. Two new minors remain; writing them up. ## What the diff does `bot/src/behaviours/scout.js` gains `findNearest` (name → `{name, position, distance}` / `null` / `'unknown'`) over the pre-existing `findNearestBlock` scan, whose defaults move to radius 48 / count 64; `bot/src/index.js` extracts the inline chat listener into an exported `handleChat` and adds a `find me <block>` branch that replies with one line and never touches the pathfinder; tests and one README line follow. That matches bead idkcraft-3nt.7 point for point. **Round 1 verification:** both minors are really fixed — `scout.js:62` no longer says "future", and `scout.test.js:251` adds a non-integral fixture. Neither is a repeat finding. **What I checked and found clean:** `handleChat` is synchronous end to end (`bot.findBlocks` is sync in mineflayer 4.39), so the tick loop has no new un-awaited promise; every throwing call inside it is wrapped, so the chat listener cannot reach `fatal()`; the listener is registered once in `main()`, not per tick; the command sets no pathfinder goal and shares no state with `makeScout`'s `seen` set, so follow/scout arbitration is untouched; no brain call is added, so the no-player cost guard is intact; no hostname, domain or IP anywhere in the diff. The 43 added lines in `index.js` are 11 moved plus ~14 of command logic — proportionate for three reply shapes. **Two minors:** 1. `resolveBlockIds` builds a fixed candidate list `[name, <base>_ore, deepslate_<base>_ore]`, which misses the two registry ores that do not follow that pattern. I checked `minecraft-data`: `nether_gold_ore` and `nether_quartz_ore` are the exceptions. So `find me quartz` answers `unknown block: quartz`, and `find me gold` standing on nether gold ore answers `no gold within 48 blocks`. The bead specified "any block name containing `<name>_ore`", which would have matched both. The helper predates this branch — this bead is what puts it in fron...

findings.title: 'find me quartz' and nether gold are unreachable: variant list misses nether_*_ore
findings.body:
`resolveBlockIds` resolves a player's word to ids by trying exactly three candidates: `[blockName, <base>_ore, deepslate_<base>_ore]` (scout.js:70). I enumerated the block registry via the bundled `minecraft-data`: every ore follows that pattern except `nether_gold_ore` and `nether_quartz_ore`.

Concrete failures, both reachable from the new chat command at index.js:156:
- A player types `find me quartz`. Candidates are `quartz` (an item, not a block), `quartz_ore` and `deepslate_quartz_ore` — none exist in `blocksByName`, so `ids` is empty and `findNearestBlock` returns `'unknown'`. The bot replies `unknown block: quartz` while standing in a Nether tunnel lined with `nether_quartz_ore`.
- A player in the Nether types `find me gold`. Only `gold_ore` and `deepslate_gold_ore` resolve, neither generates in the Nether, so the bot replies `no gold within 48 blocks` next to visible `nether_gold_ore`.

The bead's matching rule is "exact match first, else any block name containing '<name>_ore'", which matches both of these; the fixed three-candidate list is narrower than what the bead asked for. `resolveBlockIds` itself came in with idkcraft-3nt.4 and this diff only re-worded its comment — but until this bead it had no caller, so this change is what makes the gap player-visible. Impact is contained: typing the full registry name (`find me nether_quartz_ore`) still works.
findings.fix: In `resolveBlockIds`, after the three exact candidates, fall back to scanning `Object.keys(byName)` for names ending in `_ore` that contain `${base}_ore`, which picks up `nether_gold_ore` and `nether_quartz_ore` without new abstraction. Add one test asserting `findNearest(bot, 'quartz')` resolves `nether_quartz_ore`.

findings.title: Rounding test only pins one direction — Math.ceil still passes every test
findings.body:
The round-1 fix added `rounds non-integral Euclidean distance to nearest integer` (scout.test.js:251) with a block at (3,64,5) and mock origin (0,64,0): sqrt(34) ≈ 5.83, asserted as 6. That fractional part is above .5, so the assertion only distinguishes round-down implementations. Grepping every `distance` assertion in the file, there are exactly two: 10 (from (6,64,8), an exact integer) and this 6. Replacing `Math.round` at scout.js:106 with `Math.ceil` leaves all 60 tests green.

Defect this misses: the bot's real position is fractional in-game, so a vein at a true distance of 5.1 blocks would be reported as `coal_ore at ... (6 blocks)` under `Math.ceil` — the same class of off-by-one the round-1 finding was raised to prevent, just in the other direction. The distance number is one of the three fields in the only line this bead produces.

This is a gap in the fix, not a regression: the shipped code uses `Math.round` and is correct today.
findings.fix: Add a second fixture whose fractional part is below .5 — e.g. a block at (5,64,1) from origin (0,64,0) is sqrt(26) ≈ 5.10 — and assert `res.distance === 5`.
